task_text:
agentd: mask verify.json as the platform scans it, and alias whole paths only (W-31)

Review 237 of 9d16b6f:

A: cleaning the strings did not clean the bytes the platform scans. The
JSON encoder's escapes complete H8's drive-letter form: "C:<" is written
"C:\u003c", and a control character, U+2028 or an invalid byte after a
colon likewise starts with a backslash. handIn now marshals and then runs
localpath.MaskJSON, which puts a space after such a colon. It inserts only
after the colon, so no escape is split and the document stays valid
(masking the JSON with Mask, as the review proposed, would cut "\u001a"
in two). If H8 still matched or the JSON were invalid, the outputs are
withheld rather than the whole result refused.

B: the alias regexp had no left boundary and a loose right one, so
"/vendor/x/a1", "https://h/x/a1", "/x/a1+backup" and "/x/a1é" were taken
for the checkout "/x/a1", and "/x/a1/x/f" was rewritten twice. A
directory now counts only as a whole path: after the start or a character
that cannot be part of a path, and before a separator, the end or a
character that ends a path in tool output. One pattern, longest first,
replaced by index, so the aliases are no longer replacement templates.

C: Mask's loop-bound comment now counts "~/" pairs too.

Tests: TestMaskJSON, TestHandInMasksWhatEscapesComplete,
TestPathRewriteTakesWholePathsOnly; each fails with its fix taken out.

// api/internal/agentd (package agentd)

task_text:
agentd: configuration in nested repositories is seen; stale check indexes go (W-31)

Review 241 (narrow confirmation of 240) left one A and two C. The Owner
(2026-10-17 12:3x): fix them, prove with regression tests, no further review.

A1  git stops at a nested repository and names its directory, so
    configuration inside one (in an ignored directory, or added as a
    gitlink) was not seen. Such directories, and the directories among the
    changed paths, are now walked (no symlinks followed, .git skipped). The
    top-level file names are listed with --directory, so a top-level
    directory named cli.json is one entry, walked rather than printed
    file by file. Directories count by name (.cursor, .codex, .claude,
    .gemini); files by the full list.
C   a check killed with its agentd leaves its index; indexes and locks older
    than ten minutes, and the fixed-name ones of the previous version, are
    removed before a check.
C   the outcome follows the journal even when the check's result cannot be
    journalled.

Tests: TestUnwantedChangesReview241 (nested repository in an ignored
directory, one added as a gitlink, a 2000-file directory named cli.json),
TestChangesRemovesStaleIndexes, TestCheckOutcomeWhenTheJournalFails; each
fails with its fix taken out.

task_text:
agentd: the installer goes on only when launchctl print says the service is gone (review 203 A1)

The wait took any failing launchctl print for a service launchd had let
go of, so a print that failed for another reason replaced the plist and
bootstrapped into the same race. Only exit 113, "Could not find service"
(measured on macOS 26.6; 0 is still there, 64 a bad target), goes on;
any other failure stops with the old plist in place and says why.
TestInstallWaitsForLaunchdToLetGo runs the installer's own lines from
bootout to bootstrap against a stub launchctl.

agentrt actions: a result needs its exit code; entries read from Redis are held to the format (review 263 B1, B2) (W-31)

conform() checks one action the same way on the way in (Normalize) and out of Redis (entries): a known kind, a readable target, a time, an exit code on results and only there; a long target is cut and marked. Review 263: no A; both B fixed, each with a test that fails on the old code (a result without a code, five foreign entries, a long foreign target).

agentrt: nothing after the last flush wherever it falls; any ref's peeled line; an empty repository's line alone (review 206)

A1: the check after the last flush read bufio's buffer, so a flush that
ended the buffer (at 4096 bytes) let what followed through. The parser now
reads the body itself and nothing may be left after the last flush.
A2: a peeled line was allowed only under refs/tags/, but any ref may point
at an annotated tag and git advertises its peeled line (refs/pull/9/head^{}
from real git), so one such ref stopped every persist of the repository.
A peeled line is now allowed for any ref, right after the ref it peels, as
git writes it. An empty repository's capabilities^{} line must be its only
one.

lineage: an agent commit lands at the commit whose trailer its Change-Id is (review 211)

The landed SHA came from where the id first appears on main: a newer
squash that only names it in its body won, and a trailer in lower case
(parsed case-insensitively) left it empty. The main index now keeps, per
trailer, the commit that carries it, from the same parse; an agent commit
lands there. Body matches for a delivery branch still use anyCID.

agentrt sources: record version v3 so a complete v2 record gains its digests (review 170 B1) (W-31 2.2, TD-343)

Review 170, the narrow confirmation of 167's fixes, found no A: A1 and B2
fixed; B1 fixed for new records only. A v2 record written before a build's
owed digest counted as missing could be marked complete without it; v3
builds such a record again once while its run exists. No v2 record exists
in any environment (the branch was never deployed); the bump is the
reviewer's minimal fix. TestCompleteV2RecordGainsItsDigests (red with
the version left at v2).

fix(agentthreads): an ended session stays idle; only a session of the same vendor supersedes (TD-317)

Review 128: a session that had ended its turn became superseded and showed as in progress. Also the
coordinator's ruling: a session of another vendor that carries the same sidebar id is a job started from that
thread's shell, not its successor. Tests for both and for the re-check in the marking path; each planted
violation fails its test.

agentrt: a branch head only from a whole, well-formed advertisement (review 204)

A1: the reader stopped at the last flush, so an answer cut short after it
(Content-Length beyond the body), one with more after it, or one past the
bound before it, read as whole and could refuse a done result. The body is
now read to its end within the bound, and nothing may follow the last flush.
A2: a ref line was held only to an object id and a name. Every line is now
a ref by git's rules (check-ref-format), HEAD, a tag's peeled line, or an
empty repository's one capabilities^{} line; only that line has the zero
id, only the first carries a NUL, and no ref is advertised twice.
Each failure is an error of the platform, which agentd retries, whether
the branch is in the advertisement or not.

Review 238 (narrow confirmation of 237): A and C closed; B left one case.
A colour sequence right before or after a path ("\x1b[4m/x/a1/a.ts",
tsc's "\x1b[96m/x/a1/a.ts\x1b[0m:3:1") hid the path's boundaries, so
0f6aab3 no longer aliased what 9d16b6f had. withoutLocalPaths now drops
ANSI SGR sequences first; nobody reads verify.json in a terminal. The
coloured cases join TestPathRewriteTakesWholePathsOnly, which fails
without the change.

fix(volatility): the ATM IV snapshot fallback names its day both ways

fetch_snapshot_iv_rows_for_date filtered only on
DATE(timezone('America/New_York', snapshot_ts)) = day. An expression
cannot prune partitions, so every call scanned all eight of
option_snapshot's. It now also bounds snapshot_ts to the New York day,
[00:00, next 00:00), passed as instants.

The expression is kept on purpose. It is the view's own join key, so
an equality on it gives stock_daily.bar_date a constant, and stock_daily
is pruned to one partition and probed by index. A snapshot_ts filter
alone loses that; the plugin doctor's chain-spot probe, filtered that
way, hashed all of stock_daily twice (69s).

Measured read-only on bifrost_golden_source, 2026-09-28:
- plans for 4 dates (known to stats, today, empty, last month), with
  and without a symbol list: one snapshot partition instead of eight,
  stock_daily index-joined, no hash join, same shape on every date;
- output identical by md5 on 3 dates x 2 variants (253,591 and 54,540
  rows; today 0 on both, no close yet);
- 2026-09-25, median of 7 interleaved with order swapped: no symbol
  list 8.39s -> 7.09s, 655 symbols 9.62s -> 4.64s, new faster in every
  round. Without a list the current month's partition is still read
  whole: no index leads with snapshot_ts.

The path has written 0 rows to date: all 1,260,252 rows of
features.option_metric_atm_iv_daily are reconstructed.

Gates in a clean worktree: ruff and sqlfluff clean; pytest 1371 passed,
9 skipped. The new test fails on the old code.

fix(corporate-actions): a name with no rows is the vendor's answer, not a gap (B4.tail)

The feed panel said "N carry nothing at all" and counted one-row names as
"Backfilled thinly" (amber), reading them as reached but not backfilled.
Measured after the 09-29 backfill, the vendor's answer is complete for
those names: CBRS, FN, HIMS, NBIS, NNE, RKLB answer 0 rows (no dividend,
no split) and CAOS one split.

- feedReach: silent -> noneOnRecord, shallow -> oneOnRecord, docs say what
  they are.
- Panel: "Names with events" (sub: "vendor answered none on record for N:
  …"), "One event on record" (sub: "the vendor's whole answer: …", no amber).
- A failed read stays apart (feedUnread, left out of every count); its strip
  now says unread is not "none on record".

fix(research): a Pine signal too new for a return is not dimmed as cooldown (B7)

Measured on research 0.201.0: signal-stats detail sends counted_<h> false
for a signal with no bar yet at that horizon, the same as one inside an
earlier signal's cooldown. The report dimmed the newest sessions as "not
counted"; they now show — until their returns are in.

rules: the instance metrics loader stops restarting itself

Owner report (PROD 2026-09-28, after 15d1475f): "Reading fills… 36 still
loading" never resolved. 15d1475f treated the 36 as slow; they were stuck.
Measured on PROD: 1312 requests in 13 s covering only 10 distinct
instances — the same two chunks fetched 65 times.

The loop was self-exciting. useInstanceMetrics keyed its effect on
[sessionKey, ids] — ids an array memoised on the caller's `instances`.
Trade › Rules parsed its selection fresh from the URL every render, so
detail → scopedInstances → ids were new arrays with identical content;
every landed chunk re-rendered the page, the new array restarted the
effect at chunk 0, and the loop never passed chunk 2.

- useInstanceMetrics: keyed on the ids' *content* (idsKey string); the
  effect depends on sessionKey alone. A regression test hands a new array
  of the same ids on six re-renders and asserts each instance is fetched
  exactly once — verified red on the old code, green on the fix.
- TradeRulesPage: sel memoised on the raw ?pick= param (stops the cascade
  at its source, for every memo keyed on it).
- A failed read gets its own group ("Couldn't read fills") — 15d1475f
  would have parked status:error rows in loading forever.

Same measure on :5173 after: 41 requests / 1.2 s, 41 distinct instances,
8 symbol groups summing to 41, no loading group left.

Gates: tsc · eslint 0 errors · vitest 3057 · build · legacy-css.

Commissions are signed as IB books them: a rebate comes back in

Nine places took |commission|, so a rebate (a negative commission) was
charged as a cost: the FIFO pairs (computeBackendOptPairsFromExecutions,
computeOptPairsFromExecutions), a pair split into legs
(matchPairLegCashFlows), an option fill's cash flow
(ledgerOptionExecutionCashFlowSigned), the day's commission strip, the
Trade page's fallback cash, and the fee columns on Fills, On the fly and
a day's records, plus the Commissions reading.

Measured on DEV and PROD (519 fills each): every Flex fill with a
commission satisfies net_cash = ±premium − commission, the 15 negative
ones included, so negative means rebate. The tests that pinned "negative
is a cost either way" had no source behind them and now pin the measured
rule; new rebate tests (invented figures) fail on the old code.

On DEV the bulk options calendar now equals core 0.36.2's OPT pair
calendar on all 41 days of 2026-06..09 (two days had been off by cents).

Rebased onto TD-19 (6df7e0ed): performanceDayRecords.test.ts keeps
origin's label rename (s.Fills, was s.Trades) with this commit's signed
commission expectation (−1 for a 1.5 cost and a 0.5 rebate). TD-30's
−|q| sell quantities (e8953585) are untouched; nothing here reads a sign
from the quantity.

task_text:
gitea-primary step 1: the probe compares Gitea's words whole; a pull request opened without an answer is found and closed (W-31)

Review 255 (second round) found no A; its B and C are fixed:

- C: a refusal matched Gitea's words as a substring of all the output,
  so "protected branch main-other" passed for main and a longer merge
  message passed for the merge whitelist. One "remote: Gitea:" line must
  now equal the rule's words exactly, and the merge needs HTTP 405 with
  the message "User not allowed to merge PR" (Gitea 1.21's
  ErrUserNotAllowedToMerge); anything else fails the probe for a person
  to read.
- B: when the answer to opening the pull request was lost, a pull
  request Gitea had opened stayed open unmentioned. It is looked up by
  base and head and closed (read back); if the lookup fails the probe
  says there may be one open.

Tests: 15; 3 of the 4 new ones fail on ae45a18 (the fourth, nothing
opened, already passed there).
